mainTopic: What the משנה's 'presumed pure during ימי זיבה' teaches: four explanations, and רב פפא's question about caution on a day that is not a fixed וסת
overview: The משנה rules that a woman who skipped her בדיקה stays טהורה, unless the time of her וסת arrived. In that case she is טמאה, but רבי מאיר says a woman in hiding stays pure, because fear stops bleeding. People counting clean days after a discharge are presumed טמא. The גמרא asks what practical law comes from the משנה's line that a woman is presumed pure during the ימי זיבה. רב יהודה says it means she needs no בדיקה. רב חסדא says it means that even רבי מאיר permits a woman without a וסת to her husband during those days, and the גמרא defends this by filling in missing words in the משנה. רבא says it means she does not make things impure backward מעת לעת, but a ברייתא refutes him. שמואל says it means she cannot set a fixed וסת during ימי זיבה, and אביי proves to רב יוסף that he himself once taught this. רב פפא then asks whether she must still be careful on such a day, gets no answer, and begins to work it out from a משנה; his reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Skipping the check does not make her impure
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a woman who did not do a בדיקה remains טהורה, whether she skipped it by mistake, by force, or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did not check herself, whether by mistake, because she could not, or even on purpose, she is still pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says that simply not checking does not make a woman impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her status of being presumed pure stays in place. Only an actual check that finds blood would change it. The reason she skipped the check makes no difference, even if she skipped it on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: She examined herself (from בְּדִיקָה, a self-check for blood)
She acted by mistake, without meaning to
She was forced or prevented by circumstances beyond her control
She acted on purpose
Ritually pure

steps.whyThisMatters: This line becomes the basis of the גמרא's challenge later in step 7.

phrases.english: If she sat and did not examine herself,
phrases.notes: "Sat" here just means she went along without doing the check.

phrases.english: whether by mistake, or because she was prevented,
or she deliberately did not examine herself,
she is pure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failing to check, for any reason, does not make a woman impure.

steps.title: When her expected period time arrives
steps.stepSummary: If the time of her וסת arrived and she did not check, she is טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the time of her usual period came and she did not check, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where not checking does make her impure: the day her period is expected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women usually see blood at the time of their וסת. So if she did not check then, we assume she bled. This is the opposite of the general rule in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of her regular, expected period
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 1. On ordinary days, skipping the check leaves her pure. Only at the time of her וסת does skipping it make her impure.

phrases.english: If the time of her period arrived,
and she did not examine herself,
she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the general rule of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If her וסת time came and she did not check, she is impure.

steps.title: A woman in hiding stays pure
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a woman in hiding whose וסת time came and who did not check stays טהורה, because fear stops bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: if she was hiding from danger when her period time came and she did not check, she is pure, because fear pushes away blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds an exception to step 2: a woman who is hiding in fear stays pure even at her וסת time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 assumed she bled because that is normal at her וסת time. רבי מאיר says intense fear stops the flow, so that assumption does not hold for someone in hiding.

keyTerms.meaning: In hiding, for example from danger
Fear, terror
Drives away the blood (stops the flow)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
If she was in hiding,
and the time of her period arrived, and she did not examine herself,
she is pure,
because fear drives away blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה בְּמַחֲבֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman in hiding stays pure even at her וסת time, because fear stops bleeding.

steps.title: Those who already had a discharge are presumed impure
steps.stepSummary: During the days of the זב and זבה, and for a שומרת יום כנגד יום, someone who did not check is presumed טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the days of a זב and זבה, and a woman who keeps a clean day for a day, these are presumed impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by saying that people who already had a discharge and are counting clean days do not get the presumption of purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people already saw a discharge, so their starting point is impurity. Without a check proving they are clean, they stay presumed טמא. This is the reverse of the ordinary woman in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had an abnormal discharge and must count seven clean days
A woman who had abnormal bleeding outside her normal period
A woman who saw blood during the ימי זיבה and must keep one clean day for that day
Presumed to be impure

steps.whatToRemember: An ordinary woman who skips a check stays pure. At her וסת time she is impure, unless she is in hiding according to רבי מאיר. Someone already counting clean days after a discharge stays impure without a check.

phrases.english: But the days of the zav and the zava,
phrases.notes: This means the seven clean days they must count after their discharge.

phrases.english: and a woman who watches a day for a day,
these are presumed impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: these people are presumed impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב, a זבה, and a שומרת יום כנגד יום who did not check are presumed impure.

steps.title: What practical law does the presumption of purity teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what practical law comes from the משנה's statement that a woman is presumed pure during the ימי זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: For what practical law was this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks what the משנה's earlier line, that she is presumed pure, means in practice. This question sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling her "presumed pure" could have different practical results. The גמרא wants to know exactly which law follows from it.

keyTerms.meaning: For what practical law? What does this teach us in practice?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
For what halakha?
phrases.notes: This refers to an earlier line in the משנה, before our text starts, which says she is presumed pure during the ימי זיבה.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law follows from the משנה calling her presumed pure during the ימי זיבה.

steps.title: She does not need a check
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the presumption of purity teaches that she does not need a בדיקה during these days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it comes to tell us that she does not need to check herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question of step 5: "presumed pure" means she does not have to check at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, the presumption is strong enough that no check is required, not even at the outset. This answer will be challenged next.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not need an examination

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
To say that she does not require an examination.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The presumption of purity means she does not need a בדיקה.

steps.title: The later clause implies she should check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה. The סיפא says "she sat and did not check," which implies that she should check לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the later part of the משנה says "she sat and did not check" and is still pure, that shows that from the start she does need to check!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's answer using the wording of the משנה's own later clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "she sat and did not check" sounds like the משנה is describing something done after the fact, a woman who failed to do what she should have. That suggests she was supposed to check from the start, which contradicts רב יהודה's claim that no check is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of the משנה
By inference, it follows that
From the outset, ideally, before the fact

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not that she becomes impure. Everyone agrees she stays pure after the fact. The question is only whether she should check in the first place.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
"She sat and did not examine herself,"
it can be inferred that she requires examination from the outset!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that she does not need a בדיקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording "sat and did not check" describes an after-the-fact situation, which implies that checking is required לכתחילה.

steps.title: The latter clause is about the days of נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב יהודה. The סיפא, which implies she should check, refers to ימי נדה. During the eleven ימי זיבה she needs no בדיקה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter part of the משנה is talking about ימי נדה. Read the משנה like this: for all eleven days she is presumed pure and does not need to check. But during her ימי נדה she does need to check. Still, if she sat and did not check, whether by mistake, because she could not, or even on purpose, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה. It says the 'she should check' part of the משנה is about a different time period, ימי נדה, not ימי זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 7 assumed the whole משנה was about ימי זיבה. By moving the סיפא to ימי נדה, the 'check' requirement no longer clashes with רב יהודה's rule that no בדיקה is needed in ימי זיבה. Even in ימי נדה, failing to check does not make her טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
The seven days of the woman's regular period
The eleven days of זיבה that follow the days of נדה
She acted by mistake
She was prevented by circumstances beyond her control
She acted on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two time periods. 'ימי נדה' are the seven days of her regular period. 'ימי זיבה' are the eleven days after them. The answer works by assigning the two halves of the משנה to these different periods.

phrases.english: In the latter clause we have arrived at the days of נדה,
and this is what it is saying:
all eleven days she is presumed pure,
and she does not need a check,
but during the days of her נדה, she needs a check.
If she sat and did not check,
whether by mistake or because she could not,
or she purposely did not check, she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by assigning the סיפא to ימי נדה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה: רישא is about ימי זיבה, סיפא is about ימי נדה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'she sat and did not check' clause is about ימי זיבה, so checking is required there
steps.terutzMaskana: Checking is required only in ימי נדה; in ימי זיבה no בדיקה is needed, as רב יהודה said

steps.title: רב חסדא: the line is needed for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives a different explanation of the משנה's 'presumed pure in ימי זיבה.' It teaches that רבי מאיר forbids a woman without a וסת only during ימי נדה. During ימי זיבה she is presumed pure even according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this line is needed only for רבי מאיר, who said that a woman without a fixed cycle may not be with her husband. That applies only during her ימי נדה. During her ימי זיבה she stays in her presumption of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new answer to step 5's question about what practical law the משנה's 'presumed pure' line teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'no בדיקה needed' (רב יהודה), רב חסדא says the line limits רבי מאיר's strict rule. A woman with no fixed cycle is forbidden only during ימי נדה, when bleeding is likely. In ימי זיבה even she is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this case)
A woman who has no fixed menstrual cycle
To be intimate with her husband
These words apply (only) to...
The eleven days after the days of נדה

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is needed only according to רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's line that she is presumed pure in ימי זיבה, which step 5 asked about.

phrases.english: who said: a woman who has no fixed cycle
is forbidden to be with her husband.
That applies during her days of נדה,
but during her days of זיבה
she stands in her presumption of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רב חסדא אמר לא צריכא אלא לרבי מאיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 5, different from רב יהודה's
steps.terutzResolutionType: New practical application of the משנה's line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר forbids a woman without a וסת at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to רבי מאיר, she is permitted during ימי זיבה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line teaches that even according to רבי מאיר, a woman without a וסת is forbidden only in ימי נדה and stays presumed pure, and permitted, in ימי זיבה.

steps.title: Then why must he divorce her forever?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. If she is permitted in ימי זיבה, why does רבי מאיר say the husband must divorce her and never take her back?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why did רבי מאיר say he must divorce her and may never take her back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's answer by pointing to another ruling of רבי מאיר that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the husband must divorce a woman without a וסת. If she were permitted for eleven days each cycle, they could just stay married and be together on those days, so the harsh divorce rule seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you said is true)
He must divorce her and never take her back

phrases.english: If so,
why did רבי מאיר say:
he must divorce her and never take her back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי אמאי אמר רבי מאיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that רבי מאיר permits her in ימי זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there are permitted days, divorce should not be required

steps.title: Divorce is a safeguard against mistakes
steps.stepSummary: The divorce is required in case they come to be together during ימי נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps she will come to a mistake during ימי נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The divorce is a protective fence, not a sign that she is forbidden in ימי זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She really is permitted during ימי זיבה. רבי מאיר still requires divorce because, if they stay married, they might slip and be together during ימי נדה, when she is truly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / lest
A mishap; coming to sin by mistake

phrases.english: Lest she come to a mishap
during the days of נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Divorce shows she is forbidden at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: She is permitted in ימי זיבה; divorce only guards against mistakes in ימי נדה

steps.title: The משנה speaks about a woman with a וסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא again. The סיפא mentions 'the time of her וסת came,' so the משנה must be about a woman who has a fixed cycle, not one without.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the latter clause teaches 'the time of her cycle came and she did not check,' it shows that we are dealing with a woman who has a fixed cycle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב חסדא from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא read the line as being about a woman without a וסת. But the סיפא speaks of 'the time of her וסת,' which shows the משנה is about a woman with a fixed cycle. So how can the רישא be about a woman without one?

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer
We are dealing with
The time her period is expected

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:
"The time of her cycle came and she did not check,"

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דִּבְאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת עָסְקִינַן!
phrases.english: this shows we are dealing with a woman who has a fixed cycle!

steps.triggerLanguage: הא מדקתני סיפא הגיע שעת וסתה ולא בדקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב חסדא, this time from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reading that the משנה is about a woman without a וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא mentions her וסת time, so the whole משנה seems to be about a woman with a fixed cycle

steps.title: The משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing a clause. It should be read as: all eleven days she is presumed pure and permitted to her husband, but in ימי נדה she is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is how it should read: all eleven days she is presumed pure and permitted to her husband, but during ימי נדה she is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by adding a missing clause to the משנה. The added clause is about a woman without a וסת, and the סיפא can then go on to a woman with one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the added words, the משנה first teaches the case of a woman without a fixed cycle. She is permitted to her husband during the eleven days and forbidden in ימי נדה, as רבי מאיר holds. The mention of 'her וסת' in the סיפא no longer contradicts רב חסדא, because it belongs to a separate case.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה is missing words and must be filled in
And this is how it teaches
She is permitted to her husband

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of 'presumed pure in ימי זיבה.' רב יהודה says it means no בדיקה is needed. רב חסדא says it means that even according to רבי מאיר, a woman without a וסת is permitted to her husband during the eleven days. To make his reading work, he fills in missing words in the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חסורי מחסרא' does not mean the משנה is wrong. It means the משנה is written briefly, and the גמרא spells out words that are understood.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words,
and this is how it teaches:
all eleven days she is presumed pure,
and she is permitted to her husband,
and during the days of נדה she is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 and saves רב חסדא's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is about a woman with a fixed cycle
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה includes an unstated clause about a woman without a וסת: permitted in ימי זיבה, forbidden in ימי נדה

steps.title: The rest of the corrected wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the corrected reading of the משנה. The ban in ימי נדה applies only to a woman without a fixed וסת. A woman with a fixed וסת is permitted, though she should check herself. If she did not check, she is still pure, unless her וסת time arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? About a woman with no fixed cycle. But a woman with a fixed cycle is permitted, and she needs to check herself. If she did not check, whether by mistake, because she could not, or on purpose, she is pure. If the time of her cycle came and she did not check, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the corrected wording of the משנה it began in step 13. This finishes רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 added the clause 'in ימי נדה she is forbidden.' Now the גמרא limits that clause to a woman who has no fixed וסת. Because the corrected text separates the two women, the סיפא's mention of 'the time of her וסת' no longer clashes with רב חסדא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, predictable menstrual cycle
A self-examination to check for blood
She acted by mistake, without meaning to
She was prevented by circumstances she could not control
She acted on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: This is still the corrected wording of the משנה, not a new opinion. The גמרא is spelling out how the משנה should read so that רב חסדא's explanation works.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
About a woman who has no fixed cycle;
but if she has a fixed cycle, she is permitted,
and she needs to examine herself.
If she sat and did not examine herself,
whether by mistake or because she could not,
or on purpose did not examine herself, she is pure.
If the time of her cycle arrived
and she did not examine herself, she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the corrected wording that step 13 began.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא's 'time of her וסת' seemed to show the whole משנה is about a woman with a fixed cycle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban in ימי נדה is for a woman without a וסת. The 'time of her וסת' line is about a woman who has one.

steps.title: If only the last clause names רבי מאיר, the first clause is not his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The משנה says 'רבי מאיר אומר' only in the סיפא. That suggests the רישא is not רבי מאיר, yet רב חסדא explained the רישא according to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last clause is רבי מאיר, the first clause is not רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's reading. It argues that naming רבי מאיר only at the end shows the earlier part belongs to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's whole answer assumes the רישא is רבי מאיר's view. But a משנה usually names a sage only when his view differs from what came before it. So a סיפא marked 'רבי מאיר אומר' implies the רישא is another תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
The last clause of a משנה

phrases.english: But from the fact that the last clause is Rabbi Meir,
it follows that the first clause is not Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, רֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the corrected reading again, this time on who the author is.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the רישא follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming רבי מאיר only in the סיפא implies the רישא is another תנא's view, so it cannot be used to explain רבי מאיר's ruling.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר; the last clause is a contrast case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה is רבי מאיר. 'If her וסת time came and she did not check, she is impure' refers to a woman who was not hiding. רבי מאיר rules that a woman who was hiding is pure, because fear stops the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר, and this is what it means: if she was not hiding, and the time of her cycle came, and she did not check, she is impure. For רבי מאיר says: if she was hiding, and the time of her cycle came, and she did not check, she is pure, because fear drives away the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It shows that 'רבי מאיר אומר' in the סיפא is not a dispute. It explains the case just before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'רבי מאיר אומר' introduce the opposite case (a woman in hiding) that shows why the plain case is impure. So the name does not mark a new opinion, and the רישא can still be רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole of it, meaning the entire משנה
'And this is what it is saying': the גמרא is about to reread the text
A hiding place, such as hiding from danger
Fear drives away the blood, so bleeding is delayed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, the whole משנה is רבי מאיר. The named clause about hiding is a contrast case, not a separate opinion.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Meir,
and this is what it is saying:
If she was not in hiding
and the time of her cycle arrived
and she did not examine herself, she is impure,
for Rabbi Meir says:
If she was in hiding
and the time of her cycle arrived
and she did not examine herself, she is pure,
because fear drives away the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15's question about who the author is.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the named clause explains the case before it rather than disagreeing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'רבי מאיר אומר' marks a disagreement, so the רישא belongs to another תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר. The hiding case shows why a woman who was not hiding is impure.

steps.title: רבא: presumed pure means no backward impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different explanation of 'presumed pure' in ימי זיבה. It means that if she sees blood then, she does not make things impure backward for the past 24 hours (מעת לעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה comes to teach that she does not make things impure for the twenty-four hours before.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to read the משנה's words 'presumed pure.' He reads them as being about backward impurity, not about being permitted to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא read 'presumed pure' as 'permitted to her husband.' רבא reads it as a rule about purity of objects. If she sees blood in ימי זיבה, we do not worry that blood came out earlier, so what she touched in the past 24 hours stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A 24-hour period; backward impurity going back one full day
Makes things impure

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is to say that she does not impart impurity for the previous twenty-four hours.
phrases.notes: He is explaining the משנה's words 'presumed pure' in ימי זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation of the same phrase that רב יהודה and רב חסדא explained, answering the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different explanation of what the משנה is teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think 'presumed pure' teaches something about checking (רב יהודה) or about being permitted to her husband (רב חסדא).
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Presumed pure' means no backward impurity (מעת לעת) when she sees blood in ימי זיבה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Presumed pure' in ימי זיבה means that if she sees blood then, she does not make things impure backward for 24 hours (מעת לעת).

steps.title: A ברייתא says even a day-for-day woman makes things impure backward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with a ברייתא. A נדה, a זבה, a שומרת יום כנגד יום and a יולדת all make things impure backward for 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A menstruating woman, a זבה, a woman who watches a day for a day, and a woman who gave birth all make things impure for the previous twenty-four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יום כנגד יום is a woman who saw blood during ימי זיבה. רבא said blood in ימי זיבה brings no backward impurity. The ברייתא says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood one or two days in ימי זיבה and must watch for a clean day
A woman who saw blood three days in a row during ימי זיבה
A woman who gave birth

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A menstruating woman, and a zava,
and a woman who watches a day for a day,
and a woman who gave birth,
all of them impart impurity for the previous twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's explanation from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that blood in ימי זיבה brings no backward impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says a שומרת יום כנגד יום, whose bleeding is in ימי זיבה, does make things impure backward for 24 hours.

steps.title: רבא's explanation is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is a full refutation of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רבא's explanation fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered, so רבא's reading falls. Blood in ימי זיבה does bring backward impurity (מעת לעת).

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view cannot stand

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's 'no backward impurity' reading is rejected. Even blood in ימי זיבה makes things impure backward for 24 hours.

phrases.english: A refutation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge of step 18 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's explanation is refuted. A שומרת יום כנגד יום also makes things impure backward for 24 hours.

steps.title: שמואל's explanation: no fixed cycle during ימי זיבה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא, quoting שמואל, explains that 'presumed pure' in ימי זיבה means a woman cannot set a fixed וסת during those days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: The משנה comes to teach that a woman does not set a fixed cycle during her ימי זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's explanation was just refuted. Now the גמרא offers a new explanation of the משנה, quoting שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'presumed pure' in ימי זיבה is about setting a cycle, not about impurity going backward. If she sees blood on the same day of her ימי זיבה several times, that does not create a fixed וסת.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's fixed, expected time of seeing blood
Sets or establishes a fixed cycle
The 11 days after the 7 days of נדה, when blood makes her a זבה rather than a נדה

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiyya said in the name of Shmuel:
It comes to say that she does not fix a cycle for herself
phrases.notes: 'It' is the line in the משנה about her being presumed pure in ימי זיבה.

phrases.english: during her days of ziva.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינָהּ קוֹבַעַת לָהּ וֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's explanation (step 17) was refuted (step 19), a new explanation of the same words is offered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's phrase 'presumed pure'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think 'presumed pure' means she does not make things impure backward (רבא), but that was refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Presumed pure' means her sightings in ימי זיבה do not set a fixed וסת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Presumed pure' in ימי זיבה means her sightings during those days do not set a fixed וסת.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he never heard this teaching
steps.stepSummary: When שמואל's teaching is said before רב יוסף, he says he does not know it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I have not heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reacts to שמואל's teaching and says it is new to him. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not argue with the teaching. He only says he does not know of it, which raises the question of whether it really comes from שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic statement
I have not heard it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I have not heard this teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the teaching of שמואל quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not recognize the teaching in שמואל's name.

steps.title: אביי reminds רב יוסף of the משנה he taught it on
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that he himself taught this, and quotes the משנה about a woman who changes from day 15 to day 20.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it on this משנה: If a woman usually saw blood on the fifteenth day and changed to the twentieth day, she must avoid relations on both days. If she changed twice to the twentieth day, both days are still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to prove that רב יוסף did teach this. First he quotes the משנה that the teaching was attached to, and next he will quote the teaching itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that one or two changes do not cancel an old fixed cycle. She must worry about both the old day and the new day. Only a third change sets a new cycle, so the old one takes three to fully uproot.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to it; her regular pattern
She changed (her day of seeing)
To have marital relations
This one and that one (both days)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You yourself told it to us,
and it was on this that you told it to us:
If she was used to seeing blood
on the fifteenth day,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word 'יום' a second time here; the round brackets show it's left out of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and she changed to the twentieth day,
on both this day and that day relations are forbidden.
If she changed twice to the twentieth day,
both this day and that day are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim (step 21) by placing the teaching in its original setting.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף himself taught שמואל's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a woman who changes her day of seeing from 15 to 20, which רב יוסף had commented on.

steps.title: שמואל's comment: a cycle in ימי זיבה is not fixed
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes what רב יוסף had taught: according to שמואל, the משנה is only about 15 days from immersion (22 from sighting). A cycle of 15 days from sighting falls in ימי זיבה and is not a fixed cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us on it: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They only taught this about 15 days from her immersion, which is 22 days from her sighting, because there she is in her ימי נדה. But 15 days from her sighting, when she is in her ימי זיבה, does not make a fixed cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof. He quotes the exact teaching רב יוסף once gave, and it says a woman does not fix a cycle in ימי זיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule, where the old day still counts after two changes, applies only to a cycle in her ימי נדה. A day that falls inside her ימי זיבה never became a real fixed cycle, so one change is enough to drop it. This is the same rule as in step 20, so רב יוסף did teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about...
Immersion in the מקוה
A sighting of blood
The time when a new flow makes her a נדה

steps.confusionAlert: Watch which day the count starts from. 15 days from immersion is 22 days from when she first saw (7 נדה days plus 15), which is after the 11 days of זיבה. But 15 days from her sighting lands inside the ימי זיבה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a cycle that falls during ימי זיבה is not a fixed וסת, and רב יוסף himself had taught this.

phrases.english: And you told us about it,
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא אֶלָּא חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לִטְבִילָתָהּ,
phrases.english: They taught this only about fifteen days from her immersion,
which is twenty-two days from her sighting,
because there she stands in her days of נדה.
But fifteen days from her sighting,
when she stands in her days of ziva,
she has not fixed a cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַרְתְּ לַן עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's reminder by quoting the comment on the משנה from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a woman does not fix a cycle in ימי זיבה (step 20).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's own earlier teaching in the name of רב יהודה from שמואל on the משנה of changing cycles.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: must she still be careful on that day?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא told this teaching to רב יהודה of Diskarta and asked: she does not fix a cycle in ימי זיבה, but does she still need to worry about that day?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: I said this teaching before רב יהודה of Diskarta and asked: She does not fix a cycle, fine. But what about being concerned? Should we worry about her on that day?
steps.whatsHappening: With שמואל's rule now settled, רב פפא asks a follow-up question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting a fixed cycle and simply being careful are two different things. Even if her ימי זיבה pattern is not a real וסת, maybe she should still avoid relations on that day just in case. רב פפא wants to know which it is.

keyTerms.meaning: As for fixing a cycle, she does not fix one
To be concerned or cautious
What is the law?

steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two levels: a full fixed וסת, and a weaker concern that may still require caution.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
I said this teaching
before Rav Yehuda of Diskarta,
and asked: As for fixing a cycle, she does not fix one,
but as for concern, what is the law? Should we be concerned for her?
phrases.notes: He means: must she avoid relations on that day just in case she sees blood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule proven in step 23 and asks how far it goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman whose pattern falls in ימי זיבה must still be careful on that day, even though it is not a fixed cycle.

steps.title: רב יהודה of Diskarta stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה of Diskarta does not answer רב פפא's question at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was silent and did not say anything to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from the last step gets no answer. רב יהודה of Diskarta simply stays quiet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence tells us the question is not simple and has no ready answer. This leaves the question open, and that is why רב פפא tries to solve it himself in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
And nothing at all

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵי.
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything to him.
phrases.notes: The one staying quiet is רב יהודה of Diskarta, and the one he does not answer is רב פפא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in step 24 with silence, so the question stays unresolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No answer is given, so רב פפא tries to work out the question himself in step 26.

steps.title: רב פפא tries to solve it from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says 'let us see for ourselves' and quotes the משנה: a woman used to seeing on day 15 who changed to day 20 is forbidden on both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Let us look into it ourselves. The משנה says: if she was used to seeing blood on the fifteenth day and changed to the twentieth day, both this day and that day are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts to answer his own question. He quotes the משנה as the source he plans to prove from, and the actual reasoning comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא brings back the same משנה that שמואל's rule was taught on. He wants to use its ruling, 'both days are forbidden,' to decide whether a day that cannot become a fixed וסת still calls for caution. That is exactly his question about ימי זיבה. His actual reasoning from the משנה continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see for ourselves (let us work it out)
Used to, accustomed (to seeing on a set day)
She changed (her usual day)
Both days are forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends with the משנה quote and does not draw the conclusion yet. Don't assume רב פפא has finished his proof here; the גמרא is only setting up the next move.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Let us see for ourselves,
if she was accustomed to see blood
on the fifteenth day,
and she changed to the twentieth day,
both this day and that day are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because step 25 gave no answer, רב פפא now tries to solve the question from the משנה himself.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a woman must still worry about a day that cannot become a fixed וסת (the question of step 24)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a woman used to day 15 who changed to day 20 is forbidden on both days
